noModelsEndpoint: No models found. Check the endpoint, then Refresh
noModelsSignIn: No models available. Sign in, then Refresh
refreshGateway: Refresh model list from the gateway
cloudNote: Uses your SnoutData account: there is no key to enter. Use “Test” to check it.

foundModels.one: Found {count} {provider} model. Add the ones you want.
foundModels.other: Found {count} {provider} models. Add the ones you want.

noModelsKey: No models found. Check your {provider} key.
saveLoadTitle: Save the key and load {provider}'s models
addedHelp: These show in the assistant's model menu after you Save.
noneAdded: No models added yet. Paste your key, click "Load models", then add the ones you want.
byokNote: The assistant's chat and edits go straight to {provider}, bypassing SnoutData's servers, so your key and those prompts never touch our gateway. AI completion needs a fill-in-the-middle model, which your provider may not offer, so if you switch it on it uses SnoutData's completion model through our gateway. The key is kept {place}. Use “Test” to verify it.
modelsHelp: These models can be chosen in the assistant's model menu. Toggle which ones show. Add a provider under "Active provider" below to get more.
noModelsYet: No models yet. Choose a provider below to get started.
activeHelpByok: Where the assistant's models come from. Use the managed SnoutData Cloud models, or bring your own key (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Anthropic) and the assistant's chat and edits go straight to that provider, never through our servers. AI completion needs a fill-in-the-middle model, so if you switch it on it uses SnoutData's completion model through our gateway.
activeHelp: Where the assistant's models come from. Use the managed SnoutData Cloud models.
byokPitch: Point the assistant at your own OpenAI, OpenRouter, or Anthropic key. Your key stays on your machine: the assistant's chat and edits go straight to the provider, never through SnoutData's servers (AI completion needs a fill-in-the-middle model, so if you switch it on it uses SnoutData's). Part of Plus, Pro and Business.
dataAccess: What the AI may see of your data
dataAccessScope: Applies to the assistant and to coding agents connected to SnoutData. A connection can set its own level in its settings.
dataAccessDefault: Not chosen yet, so this is the default.
topTablesHelp: The top-N relevance-ranked tables for each question are described with full columns; the rest appear as name + column count. Smaller N keeps the prompt focused for local models.
autoInsertSql: Auto-insert proposed SQL into the editor
observerHelp: After a reply that proposes SQL, a model can read the exchange and suggest one fact to remember about the database. That is a second model call, on the assistant's provider, for every such reply, so it is off until you name a model here. A small, inexpensive one is enough. Leave it empty to keep it off.
toolsHelp: Choose what the assistant may do. Database tools need a connected database.
runQueriesHint: (you approve each query; writes are always refused)
runQueriesOff: Switched off by "What the AI may see of your data" above, which does not include read-only queries.
autoApproved: Auto-approved connections. Queries run without asking (set via “Always allow” on the approval prompt):
noneAsked: None. You'll be asked before each query.
askAgainTitle: Ask again before running queries here
byokCompletionNote: Your own key covers the assistant's chat and edits only. AI completion needs a fill-in-the-middle model, which your provider may not offer, so it always uses SnoutData's completion model through our gateway. When it is on, the text around your cursor, the relevant schema and some of your earlier queries on that connection are sent to SnoutData's servers.
triggerAuto: Automatic, as you type (best with a fast local model)
completionHelp: Completion uses its own dedicated model (these are separate from the chat list). It wants speed + SQL fill-in-the-middle, not raw intelligence, so a small FIM code model beats a big chat model here.
completionOff: Off. The editor still has deterministic, local schema completion ({shortcut}). Turn this on to add model-generated ghost text.
